title: Exact endian writes and selected prefix reads, with failure contracts
explanation: byteorder 1.5.0: fixed-width unsigned and signed integer writes, plus BE/LE write_f32/write_f64, write their exact bit representations in the selected endian order and preserve trailing bytes when the output is long enough; shorter buffers panic before writing. Float proofs quantify over every 32/64-bit representation, including NaN payloads and signed zeros, under explicit bit-pattern and std to_bits models. No floating arithmetic is modeled. BE/LE read_u24 additionally returns the exact unsigned24 prefix decode below2^24, and asserts on shorter input. LittleEndian from_slice_u16/u32/u64/u128 additionally leave every slice unchanged on the verified little-endian target, including empty slices and arbitrary unsigned values. The two handwritten Default methods always panic. Four unsigned variable-width readers decode the exact selected prefix under their complete byte-count/input-length guard, and assert otherwise.
trusted_assumptions: F32/F64 are explicit 32/64-bit logical patterns; two executable std to_bits models preserve those patterns as unsigned words, with checked Lean value-preservation lemmas. Guards require original writer bodies and allow no other float operation. Kani checks std bit identity for every pattern and actual released writers with 6/10-byte buffers. Connecting these Rust checks to the Lean representation is reviewed, not mechanized; Rust nightlies differ. Official translation/standard integer and slice models, Lean, and Kani/CBMC are trusted. The four original native conversion bodies make no external calls after official target-branch translation. Five unused declarations remain in the unchanged, unimported template; the provider supplies zero definitions. Guards require exact identity bodies and zero external use. Mapped audits permit only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

limitations: This covers 20 selected writer methods, six unsigned readers, four native-target unsigned identity conversions, and two handwritten Default methods, not all public APIs.
